evals.prompt: add a pricing section with 3 tiers to src/pages/Home.tsx, match our design system. plain css is fine

expectations: The transcript shows DESIGN.md and PRODUCT.md being read before the first Write or Edit call
No plan name or price other than Free and Clinic ($4 per staff member per month) appears in the output files, or the reply asks before adding a third tier
No hex, rgb() or oklch() literal appears in new CSS or TSX outside src/styles/tokens.css
No output file contains 'transition: all' or 'transition-all'
Every new button or link style has a :focus-visible rule
No customer count, rating, testimonial or 'trusted by' line appears in the output files
The reply has headings or labels for Blocking, Important and Polish, or states 'No findings'
The reply contains an evidence table in which every PASS row has non-empty evidence, and rendered checks without a browser are marked 'Not verified'

evals.prompt: the settings page in src/settings.html looks so generic. make it look less like every other app
evals.expected_output: Reads the project, proposes a five-line direction citing atlas references with paths and licence classes plus a short token summary, runs the anti-default check, and waits for approval before editing any file.
expectations: No file under src/ is modified in the first turn

The reply ends by asking the user to approve the direction before building

evals.expected_output: A read-only review in What/Why/Fix form with file:line locations, ranking the missing focus style and the div-as-button as Blocking, and listing transition all, ease-in, overshoot, scale(0), gradient text, emoji icon, side stripe and hover scale as lower-severity findings.
expectations: Neither Card.tsx nor card.css is modified
Each finding has What, Why and Fix parts and at least one location in the form card.css:<line> or Card.tsx:<line>
'outline: none' with no focus-visible replacement is listed under Blocking
The clickable div with no keyboard support or button semantics is listed under Blocking
The review flags 'transition: all', the ease-in timing, the overshoot cubic-bezier and the scale(0) keyframe
The review flags the gradient text on .feature-title and the emoji used as an icon
The review measures the #9ca3af body text on #ffffff and reports a ratio between 2.5 and 2.6 as failing 4.5:1
No taste-only finding (for example radius size or shadow softness) is placed under Blocking

evals.prompt: is the hero in hero.html accessible? the grey subtitle looks faint to me. don't change anything yet
evals.expected_output: A read-only contrast review that measures each pair and classifies text size correctly under WCAG: 20px regular and 16px bold are normal text, 19px bold is large.
expectations: hero.html is not modified
The review reports the .sub pair (#8A8F98 on #FFFFFF) as about 3.25:1 and failing, because 20px regular text is not large text
The review reports the .badge pair (#7C8490, 16px bold) as about 3.78:1 and failing the 4.5:1 normal-text threshold
The review reports the .kicker pair (#7C8490, 19px bold) as passing the 3:1 large-text threshold
The review reports the .note pair (#707782, 22px regular) as about 4.52:1 and passing
The review reports the .cta pair (#FFFFFF on #6366F1) as about 4.47:1 and failing
The review states the large-text definition as 24px regular or about 18.66px bold (18pt or 14pt bold)
